statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 16 (low), Stress 37 (moderate), Confidence 87 (high). The Sep 22 US cash session ended with a second consecutive record Nasdaq-100 close, and CME index futures are now in their 21:00-22:00Z daily maintenance break.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window is the Sep 23 US cash open at 13:30Z together with the 13:45Z S&P Global flash PMIs, where the forecast maps to WATCH. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 settles at a record 30,732.40 (+0.82%) as VIX slips to 14.21 and WTI falls 2.7% on Iran diplomacy; Sep 23 cash open plus flash PMIs flagged
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the Sep 22 US cash session at 30,732.40, up 0.82%, opening at the 30,496.43 session low and settling 38 points (0.12%) below the 30,770.63 high - a second consecutive record close. Leadership was narrow rather than broad: the S&P 500 finished essentially flat and the Dow fell 0.36%, so cross-sectional breadth conflicts with the index-level directional efficiency. The session path was driven by crude, which fell after reports that Iran signalled willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if US military pressure eased, and by the AI complex, where Meta extended gains on its Muse AI agent. Trump's UN remarks and a subsequent three-hour US-Iran meeting pushed WTI down 2.73% to $89.85 and Brent down 1.68% to $98.65. Cross-assets are supportive rather than stressed: VIX 14.21 (-4.44%), the 10-year Treasury yield near 4.97% and the 2-year near 4.75%, both little changed on the day. NQ futures last printed 31,002.00 (+0.71%), about 63 points below their own session high, before entering the CME maintenance break at 21:00Z; they reopen at 22:00Z. Against that mix, the single genuine Tail amplifier is the index-level directional efficiency into a record settlement, and it is offset by narrow breadth, a falling volatility surface, an intraday reversal on the UN headlines that made retracement available, and flat yields. Tail is therefore scored 16 (low) rather than at the block threshold, with Stress at 37 (moderate) reflecting the still-unresolved Hormuz negotiation and an active conflict backdrop. No index-relevant Nasdaq earnings fall inside the next 24 hours; Micron reports Sep 30, outside this window. Risk concentrates on the Sep 23 US cash open at 13:30Z and the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45Z, with a second leg from the Barr speech at 14:05Z and EIA inventories at 14:30Z.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 published hours are complete with no unavailable slot. Overnight Sep 21-22 held Tail 11-14 in normal conditions. Tail stepped to 21 (WATCH) at 14:00Z on the US cash open, eased to 14-17 through a mixed midday, then returned to 20-21 (WATCH) from 18:00Z as the index pressed toward its record settlement, closing the window at 19 as the cash session ended. No hour in the lookback reached the block threshold.
outlookSummary: Overnight Tail is expected to hold in a 13-15 band through Asia and early Europe in normal mode, with no scheduled US catalyst before the European morning. Scores step up through the European session and concentrate at the Sep 23 US cash open at 13:30Z and the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45Z, where the forecast reaches Tail 21 (WATCH) in event/whipsaw mode and holds 20 for the Barr and EIA second leg. The path then decays through the US afternoon as post-event price discovery is assessed, with a conditional firming to 19 into the closing hour. All future structure is conditional; no Sep 23 price path has been observed.
